sections.h2: Why is Jones County a commuter county for Macon and Milledgeville?
sections.html:
Jones County sits near the geographic center of Georgia, on the fall line, and the New Georgia Encyclopedia describes it today as a bedroom community for people who work in nearby Macon or Milledgeville. The state created the county in 1807 as its thirty-second, and it covers almost 400 square miles. Cotton and then peaches and peppers drove the early economy, but two gravel quarries are the only industry the encyclopedia singles out now.

Gray became the county seat in 1905, taking over from Clinton, whose old residences are on the National Register of Historic Places. Two battles were fought here in 1864: Sunshine Church in the summer and Griswoldville in November. Buyers who like history look at Jarrell Plantation State Historic Site, and more than 30,000 acres of worn-out cotton land across Jones and neighboring Jasper County became the Piedmont National Wildlife Refuge in the 1930s.

sections.h2: How do Jones County housing numbers compare with the rest of the region?
sections.html:
Jones County's 83.6% ownership rate and $75,500 median household income are both well above the matching Census figures for Johnson County.

With 10,786 households and an 83.6% ownership rate, most sales here are owner-occupied houses rather than rentals. The 29.8-minute average commute fits the pattern of people living in Jones County and working in Macon or Milledgeville, so buyers often compare a Gray house with options on the Bibb County side of the line.

sections.h2: Who do I call at Jones County for taxes?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner's office is at 166 Industrial Blvd. in Gray, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 417, Gray, GA 31030. It is open 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., and the phone is 478-986-6538.

  • Tax Commissioner: bills, payments, mobile home decals, timber and heavy equipment tax. Pay and search through jonescountytaxes.com.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: values, returns and exemptions, at (478) 986-6300.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: deed room in the courthouse, where you can get a copy of a warranty deed.
  • City of Gray City Hall: bills the city portion separately, at 478-986-5433.

Intangible recording tax is collected by the Clerk of Superior Court, not the tax commissioner, which matters when a buyer's lender records a security deed.

sections.h2: What are the Jones County due dates and late charges?
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property bills are generally mailed by October 1 and are due December 1. The 2025 bills went out on September 25, 2025, with a December 1, 2025 due date, and the office notes that interest accrues after close of business on the first of each month.

Interest runs at 1% per month after the due date. A penalty also attaches 90 days after the deadline, and the office's own pages disagree about its size: the property page says 5% while the FAQ says 10%. Confirm the figure before you set a payoff number. Homesteaded property with a tax liability under $500 is excused from the 90-day penalty. Unpaid taxes can be levied on, and a fifa lien can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court once they are more than 90 days late.

  • Mobile homes: bills mailed around January, due April 1, with a 10% penalty, a Magistrate Court citation or a sale of the home possible if unpaid. The 2026 bills were mailed January 29, 2026, with an April 1, 2026 due date.
  • Partial payments are accepted, but interest keeps running on the rest.
  • City of Gray: its 2024 bills were mailed October 29 and due December 29, 2024.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can a Jones County owner claim?
sections.html:
Jones County has local legislation on top of the state exemptions, and the county's page spells out the amounts as follows.

  • Standard homestead: $2,000 off the 40% assessed value, applied to county and school maintenance and operation and the state levy, not to bond debt.
  • Local school exemption: $15,000 of assessed value off school maintenance and operation and school bonds for anyone who turned 62 by January 1, with no income limit.
  • Elderly school exemption: up to $10,000 at age 62 or older when net income is $10,000 or less.
  • Elderly general exemption: up to $4,000 at 65 or older when net income of applicant and spouse is $10,000 or less.
  • Disabled veterans: up to $63,780, and the same for a surviving spouse of someone killed in an armed conflict.
  • Floating exemption: age 62 or older with gross household income of $30,000 or less, state and county tax only.

First-time homeowners should bring a copy of the warranty deed when filing, and the application must be received by April 1. The tax deferral program lets owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less postpone payment until ownership changes or the deferred amount plus interest reaches 85% of fair market value. For farmland, agricultural assessment is 30% instead of 40%, and all the preferential programs require a 10-year covenant with the assessors.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Jones County value?
sections.html:
An appeal must be made within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice, either to the county Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator, and a further appeal to superior court follows by written notice to the assessors. The Revenue Department adds that the grounds can be taxability, value, uniformity or denial of an exemption.

Returns are due between January 1 and April 1, and an owner who files nothing is treated as returning the same property at the same final value as last year. Filing a return with your own opinion of value can preserve appeal rights if the assessors change the number. Mobile home owners have 45 days after bills are mailed to contest the value, and a further 21 days from a revised notice to go to the Board of Equalization.

sections.h2: What should a Jones County seller do about taxes before closing?
sections.html:
Get a current payoff from the tax commissioner and add the city of Gray's separate bill if the house is inside city limits. The Georgia Department of Revenue notes that the owner on January 1 is responsible for the year's tax, so a sale in the spring still carries that year's bill, and the contract should say who reimburses whom.

The county reminds owners that tax bills go to the homeowner, never the mortgage company, so forward yours if a lender escrows. A buyer paying cash can close quickly, but they will still want the lien search clear, and recorded liens show up at the Clerk of Superior Court.

faqs.q: When are Jones County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 1 for real estate and business personal property, with bills generally mailed by October 1. The 2025 bills were mailed on September 25, 2025. Interest of 1% per month starts after the due date.

faqs.q: What is the Jones County local school exemption for seniors?
faqs.a: It is $15,000 of assessed value off school maintenance and operation and school bond tax for owners who reached 62 by January 1 of the tax year. The county's page says there is no income limit.

faqs.q: Where do I get a copy of my deed in Jones County?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Superior Court's deed room in the Jones County Courthouse in Gray. The tax commissioner's FAQ points owners there for a warranty deed copy.

faqs.q: How big is the penalty on late Jones County taxes?
faqs.a: The county's property page says 5% at 90 days after the due date and its FAQ says 10%. Ask the tax commissioner at 478-986-6538 which figure applies to your bill. Homesteaded property with tax under $500 is excused from the 90-day penalty.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Jones County?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $194,500 for owner-occupied homes in 2020-2024. Median gross rent was $964 and median household income was $75,500.
